question: You have a weekend project: Build a robot arm OR design an algorithm to sort a billion records in under 1 second. Which excites you more?

options.text: Robot arm — I want to see it move!
Sorting algorithm — pure mathematical elegance.

question: Your team's app is down in production at 2 AM. You're on-call. Your reaction?

options.text: Adrenaline rush — I've already SSH'd in and am reading logs.
Methodically create a runbook first, then fix calmly.

question: You discover a complex bug that will take 3 weeks to trace. How do you feel?

options.text: Excited — it's a puzzle that needs me.
Anxious — I'd rather build new features.

question: You're given 10 crore rupees to invest. Which do you pick?

options.text: Start a high-risk tech startup — huge upside.
Low-risk index funds + a safe govt job on the side.

question: You're building a new product. Your preferred role?

options.text: Writing the core engine — nobody else touches my architecture.
UX & interface — I want users to love how it feels.

question: Math class: you hit a proof you can't crack in 2 hours. You:

options.text: Stay up all night — I must solve it myself.
Collaborate and look up similar proofs to build intuition.

question: Your dream project at a big tech company:

options.text: Designing the next-gen chip architecture for AI inference.
Building the recommendation engine that serves 2 billion users.

question: Financial pressure: your family expects you to start earning ASAP. How does this change your plan?

options.text: I'll take a corporate job and build skills; passion later.
I'll hustle — internships, freelancing, startup — passion now.

question: Your team needs a leader on a vague, open-ended project with no clear spec. You:

options.text: Step up — ambiguity is where I shine.
Ask for a defined scope; I execute brilliantly within constraints.

question: If you could master one of these by next year, which?

options.text: Quantum computing fundamentals.
Building an autonomous delivery drone.

question: A recruiter offers you two options after graduation:

options.text: ₹12 LPA at a stable MNC with structured growth.
₹6 LPA + 0.5% equity at a Series A startup.

question: When you imagine your most satisfying day at work, it looks like:

options.text: Deploying code that millions of people use instantly.
Presenting a research paper that changes how the field thinks.

question: You have to pick one thing to be the best in the world at:

options.text: Machine Learning & AI research.
Embedded systems & robotics engineering.
Computer Vision + NLP + Reinforcement Learning.
VLSI Design + Power Systems + IoT Prototyping.
